Home.loose_stories: Casual stories from programmers lifes and practical knowledge in an easy form.
Home.about: We create light-hearted, humorous approach to programming. We talk about bugs that cost hours of debugging, successes after endless fixes, but most importantly we share experiences in a light, accessible way.
Home.q1: Do I have to be a programmer to join the community?
Home.a1: No, but there is a risk you will become one.
Home.q2: I code in PHP. Can I join?
Home.a2: Yes, but we will be watching you closely.
Home.q3: Do I have to pay to access the community?
Home.a3: No. But if you want to send coffee, our backend developer will be happy.
Home.q4: My code doesn't work, but there are no errors. Can you help me?
Home.a4: Sure, although the problem may be deeper. Probably the code is testing you, not you the code.

Principles.title: Our principles
Principles.code_for_people_desc: You write code for other programmers (and for yourself in half a year, when you forget what was going on here). Good standards are not an art for art's sake, but a way for others (and you) not to suffer.
Principles.new_technologies_desc: Experiments are great, until you blow up production. Novelties are not always gold - sometimes it's just a shiny trap. The balance between fresh solutions and stability is the key.
Principles.code_today: Code for today, but with tomorrow in mind
Principles.code_today_desc: Requirements change faster than JavaScript frameworks. That's why the code should be flexible and easy to expand - you never know what the future will bring (except for more changes from the Project Manager).
Principles.no_path: There is no one right path
Principles.no_path_desc: There are no sacred coding rules - there are only those that actually help. The code should work and be understandable, not look like a computer science textbook.
